item.text: {"question_id":"6B.8","answer":"During Lula’s 2023 period, the federal government enacted or initiated several equal-rights and dignity measures: it revoked a rule requiring health professionals to report rape survivors seeking abortion, resumed sexual and reproductive-health education, created a National LGBTQI+ Rights Council and mandatory federal social-name protections, created a Racial Equality Ministry, signed a racial-equality package, passed equal-pay legislation, and established a women’s-violence program whose design emphasizes integrated, humanized, non-revictimizing services (BATCH-0001-E010; BATCH-0007-E004; BATCH-0001-E037; BATCH-0016-E005; BATCH-0016-E008; BATCH-0013-E008). The housing program also formally prioritized vulnerable groups, including disabled and older people, with adapted units, and other marginalized groups (BATCH-0019-E018). These measures demonstrate legal and institutional action, but not broad practical remedy or equal access. Equal-pay legislation was not yet enforced; domestic and gender-based violence persisted or increased; protective-order decisions often exceeded the legal deadline; racial-discrimination law was not effectively enforced; police violence disproportionately harmed Black people; LGBTQI+ violence and discrimination continued; disability-access laws and employment quotas were weakly enforced; and Indigenous communities continued to experience violence, discrimination, inadequate services, and unresolved territorial conflict (BATCH-0001-E035; BATCH-0001-E009; BATCH-0016-E008; BATCH-0007-E005; BATCH-0001-E037; BATCH-0005-E027). Broader dignity and remedy concerns also included UN findings of extrajudicial executions, torture, racialized over-policing, prison overcrowding and discrimination, while CNJ research found severe prison health risks, underreported deaths, weak records, and little accountability or reparation; these findings concern state systems and do not establish Lula’s personal responsibility for each failure (BATCH-0015-E001; BATCH-0015-E006; BATCH-0018-E009; BATCH-0019-E012). Overall, the evidence supports meaningful ruler-attributed legal and institutional movement, but implementation, accessibility, enforcement, group-level outcomes, and effective remedy remained materially incomplete during the
